newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares jump 3.2 pct to new record close.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares jump 3.2 pct to new record close.

text.p: Istanbul shares jumped an average 3.2 percent amid heavy selective buys on Thursday, with the market index and trade volume reaching new records on fresh cash influx, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed at a new all-time high of 87,299.29, up 2,704.17 points from Wednesday and compared to a previous high of 84,692.20 on November 11.
Trade volume rose to a record 31 trillion lira ($311.5 million) from Wednesday's 28.11 trillion ($283 million) and compared to a previous record of 28.83 trillion on October 21.

Brokers selective activity was led by shares of largely state-owned flat steel producer Eregli amid renewed privatisation hopes as State Minister Abdullah Gul said Eregli's 25 percent stake would be put on sale in coming days.
Hectic trade in Eregli which strongly influences the market index due to the firm's large market capitalisation, made up 15.7 percent of the total turnover. It gained 2,000 lira to end at 14,500.
"Eregli played a major role in the market's gains today. There was cash entry to the market, fuelled by the recent privatisation announcements," said Nazmi Sarikaya from Disbank.
"The index pierced the 85,000 critical barrier. The new target may be 89,000," he said.
The market had failed in in three previous attempts to overcome the 85,000 resistane since late October.
